details:
WHAT IT DOES

AstroVital is an offline health-monitoring system for astronauts on the International Space Station, the Moon and Mars. Crew members log temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, SpO2, sleep, mood, stress, radiation dose and symptoms, and mark pain on a rotatable 3D body. Every reading gets a green, yellow or red status, and the body map shows each organ system at a glance.

HOW IT WORKS

An Android tablet app built in Flutter connects over Bluetooth Low Energy to our own ESP32 device: an infrared MLX90614 temperature sensor, a 4x4 keypad usable with gloves and an OLED display. All data stays on the device (SQLite), so it works with no internet.

Astro, our AI assistant, learns each astronaut's personal baseline during Earth training and compares it with readings in space, detecting deviations and trends that fixed medical limits miss. The AI can only raise a reading to yellow; red is reserved for fixed medical thresholds. Astro talks and chats offline, explains each measurement, and guides the crew step by step with protocols that the flight surgeon can edit and that cite their sources (NASA, AHA, ADA). When a reading is critical, it automatically notifies the flight surgeon's panel and checks the astronaut's consciousness every minute with varied questions, escalating if there is no answer. Every false alarm requires a reason, so Astro learns without reducing safety. The data can be exported as anonymous CSV files to retrain an optional on-device model (TensorFlow Lite) using real data only.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Communication delays of up to 20 minutes on the way to Mars mean crews must handle medical issues on their own. AstroVital gives them early detection, clear instructions and automatic escalation. On Earth, the same approach can support remote communities, polar stations and older adults living alone.

TOOLS

Flutter/Dart, SQLite, Bluetooth Low Energy, ESP32 (C++/Arduino), MLX90614 sensor, model-viewer 3D, speech-to-text and text-to-speech, TensorFlow Lite, Python/Colab for model training.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Offline operation, glove-friendly controls, privacy (no names in exports), never training on invented data, and keeping a doctor in the loop.
